summary: Large embedding upload caused apigw 5xx spike and upstream memory pressure (prod us-west)
description:
Issue summary:
During a large multipart embedding upload from DataScale Analytics (~120k vectors, ~3.2GB) to our embed endpoint in us-west, customers observed a sudden elevation in 5xx rates from the API gateway and increase in upstream serving runtime OOM/restart events. The surge started at 2025-11-02T18:10:00Z and persisted for ~18 minutes before initial mitigation.

Impact:
- DataScale saw ~40% of requests return 5xx (502/503) for the embed route during the window.
- Platform health dashboards show increased NVMe iowait and high IO latencies on a subset of hosts.
- Several serving-runtime pods showed memory pressure, one OOM kill and automatic restart.

Observed behavior:
- api-gateway returned spikes of 502 / upstream connection reset and 503 timeouts.
- Ingress proxy logs show slow reads and long tail latencies when reading request bodies.
- Host-level metrics show NVMe avg latency climbing to 50-200ms on impacted nodes and CPU steal spikes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a large embedding bulk upload (~100k vectors in a few GB multipart upload) to the customer upload endpoint in us-west.
2) Send at sustained parallelism 8-12 clients (similar to DataScale's client).
3) Observe apigw request durations and error rates; watch ingress proxy read latencies and nvme i/o metrics.
4) Check serving-runtime memory/resident set growth during backpressure.

timeline:
2025-11-02 18:09:45Z - DataScale begins large multipart upload.
2025-11-02 18:10:00Z - apigw error rate begins to climb; alert triggered (5xx > 10% baseline).
2025-11-02 18:11:00Z - SRE paged; observed nvme iowait on subset of hosts and long ingress read times.
2025-11-02 18:12:30Z - One serving-runtime pod OOM and restarts; apigw 502s increase.
2025-11-02 18:20:00Z - Support applied temporary per-tenant ingestion throttle for DataScale and enabled backpressure at ingress; 5xx rate declined.
2025-11-02 18:28:00Z - Customer confirmed reduced errors; ticket opened for root cause and follow-ups.
comments: Support (Aisha): Notified SRE and DataScale; collecting request ids and sample upload manifest.
SRE (Diego): Observed NVMe latency spike on three hosts in us-west-2 cluster; suspect localized disk saturation from concurrent background compaction + large uploads.
Customer (DataScale) reply: We kicked off a bulk migration job; can throttle if recommended. Provided start time and client IDs.
Support (Aisha): Applied temporary per-tenant bandwidth and concurrency throttle; recommended retry window and exponential backoff for clients. Monitoring shows error rate trending down.
SRE (Diego): Investigating autoscaler/eviction interplay; adding host iowait alerting and scheduling maintenance for compaction windows.
Customer (DataScale): Confirming post-mitigation uploads succeeding; will coordinate future large commits with Redwood support.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses under investigation:
- Large multipart upload caused ingress proxy slow-reads which prolonged TCP connections and increased file system pressure leading to NVMe iowait, cascading into serving runtime memory growth under backpressure.
- Background storage compact/GC coincided with heavy upload on same shard set producing IO saturation.
- Autoscaler reacted to perceived high CPU/IO latency poorly: scale decisions led to hot shard rebalancing and increased memory pressure.

Metrics/dashboards referenced:
- https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingress/ingress-read-latency?var-region=us-west
- https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/storage/nvme-iowait?var-host=i-0a1b2c3d
- Related logs: slack thread #support-ds-analytics and /incidents/2025-11-02-embed-iowait

Preliminary finding: correlation between large upload window and host-level IO saturation; need post-incident artifact collection (iostat, dmesg, kernel logs).
resolution_notes:
Mitigations performed:
- Temporary per-tenant ingest concurrency limit and rate throttle applied at API gateway for DataScale, immediately reducing error surface.
- Ingress backpressure thresholds adjusted to fail-fast smaller uploads rather than letting backpressure cascade to runtime.
- Scheduling: storage team to avoid compaction/GC on affected shard group during client bulk-window; ops to add nvme iowait alert and run iostat snapshot collection at next occurrence.

Next steps:
1) Storage team to audit background compaction scheduling and add jitter (owner: Mateo R.).
2) Autoscaler rules review to avoid scale-induced rebalancing during sustained IO pressure (owner: Priya S.).
3) Prod playbook update: recommend coordination with support for uploads >1GB; create prewarm route for bulk-embeds.
4) Post-incident analysis: collect kernel logs and nvme SMART data from impacted hosts; create postmortem doc and link to confluence.
customer_communication: Emailed DataScale within 30 minutes with summary and temporary mitigation steps; offered duty-window coordination for future large uploads and invite to postmortem.
